question.problem: The maximum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)=-4{x}_{1}^{2}+6{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+4{x}_{2}^{2},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $5.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the maximum is attained?
question.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max\{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1\}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min\{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1\}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 3 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{max}}=5:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-5I & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 3 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}]-5[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-9 & 3 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-5I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$ 

Finally, dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{10},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{max}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$
